title: Protests and marches planned in Rome against violence against women
seoTitle: Rome marches against violence against women

tea.why: Protesters are mobilizing against patriarchal violence and government policies promoting natalism.
tea.want: Participants demand bodily autonomy, self-determination, and a rejection of traditional reproductive expectations.
tea.changed: Nov 24: Organizers announced a schedule of rallies, sit-ins, and a national march in Rome for late November.

summary: Various protests, sit-ins, and a national march have been scheduled in Rome around the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. Organized by groups such as Non Una di Meno, the actions include demonstrations between Piazza Pia and Castel Sant'Angelo, neighborhood walks, sit-ins, and a national march starting from Piazza della Repubblica. According to the organizers, the mobilization aims to challenge patriarchal violence and counter government-backed natalist propaganda. The events are expected to cause local traffic disruptions and public transport deviations across the city.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Authorities and organizers outlined schedules for upcoming rallies and a national march in Rome.
